transcript.text: This is the Paper Library daily on Enhancers & 3D genome, for Tuesday, November 24.
Let's turn to Enhancers and 3D genome, with three bioRxiv preprints today.

First, from the Biswas lab: can perturbation data beat co-expression for building regulatory networks in triple-negative breast cancer? The authors combine enhancer-targeting CRISPR interference Perturb-seq data from MDA-MB-231 cells with ENCODE transcription factor binding as prior information.

On held-out CRISPRi results, the area under the precision-recall curve was about zero point eight seven, versus zero point six three for GENIE3 and zero point six eight for co-expression. Central regulators include CTCF, EP300, MYC and AP-1 factors, and their signatures were associated with survival.
The caveats: it's a single cell line, the survival cohorts are modest, and the proposed epigenetic combination treatments were only simulated, so they're candidates for experimental validation.

Second, from the Su lab: what makes human cortical progenitors different? The authors compare time-resolved paired single-nucleus RNA and ATAC profiles from human, macaque and mouse fetal cortex, and find programs enriched in human outer radial glia, including the gene RHOJ.

The highlight is an enhancer inside a RHOJ intron. The human version is more active in reporter assays than other primates' versions, partly due to a human-specific change in an AP-1 motif. Deleting it in human cortical organoids lowered RHOJ expression and impaired growth.
So AP-1 shows up twice today, in a tumor network and in human brain evolution.

Third, a methods paper from the Matera lab on normalizing CUT and RUN and CUT and Tag data without spike-ins, for perturbations that change a chromatin mark genome-wide. Their method, BASIN, uses reproducible background in IgG controls as an internal reference to scale each sample.

It stayed stable across a more than hundred-fold range of input cells, and detected the genome-wide loss of H3 K36 trimethylation in Drosophila Set2 mutants, which standard read-depth normalization hid.
One limitation: the ready-made reference panel only covers Drosophila, so other organisms need a custom panel.
The takeaway: perturbations, from CRISPRi screens to enhancer deletions, are becoming the standard test for regulatory claims, and measuring their effects well depends on careful normalization.

papers.title: BASIN: Background-Anchored Signal Normalization with Integrated Quality Control for CUT&RUN and CUT&Tag
Cross- species developmental multiomics identifies RHOJ as a regulator of human-enriched cortical progenitor states
Integrating CRISPRi perturbation responses and transcription-factor binding priors for regulatory network inference in triple-negative breast cancer
